name: Genetic Epidermal Appendage Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic Epidermal Appendage Anomaly Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of congenital malformations of epidermal appendages including hair, nails, and sweat glands
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes known to regulate epidermal appendage development
Histopathological evidence of abnormal epidermal appendage structure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital epidermal appendage malformations plus either positive family history or genetic mutation identification
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended for confirmation when available.

searchTerms: sparse or missing hair from birth
thin or fragile hair since birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypohidrosis due to sweat gland aplasia or hypoplasia

searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles
mild palm and foot skin thickening
slight keratin buildup on hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Sparse or absent eyebrows and eyelashes
searchTerms: thin or missing eyebrows and eyelashes
loss of eyebrow and eyelash hair
heat sensitivity due to low sweat

rare.symptomName: Secondary skin infections due to barrier defects
searchTerms: skin infections due to weak skin

laboratory: Possible mild elevation of inflammatory markers if secondary infection present
imaging: Not typically required; imaging may be used to exclude other syndromes
genetic: Mutations in genes regulating epidermal appendage development such as TP63, EDA, or WNT10A
other: Histopathology showing abnormal follicular and glandular structures
Clinical examination revealing characteristic appendage anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: More extensive involvement of teeth and sweat glands
Presence of systemic features such as immune deficiency
Severe nail thickening and painful plantar keratoderma

redFlags: Severe hypohidrosis leading to recurrent hyperthermia
Marked nail dystrophy with secondary bacterial or fungal infection
references: Orphanet: Genetic Epidermal Appendage Anomaly - ORPHA:183447
Wheeler et al., 2022. Genetic Disorders of Epidermal Appendages. Journal of Dermatological Science.
